To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we generated and analyzed camel ESTs, and that we have established a relational database to host and share our results.

we have generated 70,272 EST reads from two different libraries of the camel and have assembled 23,602 EST sequences, out of them 4,500 sequences have no similarity to any other known sequence in databases and the remaining sequences are functionally annotated.
we have generated 23,602 camel EST sequences and characterized them for their potential to be novel genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
establishing a camel gene database and annotation, and providing a platform for future genomic research.
sequencing, annotation and analysis of ESTs of camel.
the generation of a comprehensive set of camel ESTs, their assembly, annotation, and their availability to the public through a web portal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current study has successfully sequenced and analyzed a significant number of camel expressed genes, providing a valuable resource for further studies of camel and comparative studies.
this study has generated a significant resource of EST data for the dromedary camel.
our results represent a major contribution in the field of camel genomics and provide a starting point for the sequencing of whole camel genome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to provide an initial set of annotated EST sequences that would serve as a basis for future genome sequencing and comparative genomic studies.

we have successfully sequenced, analyzed, annotated, and made available to public domain the first large-scale EST library of camel, which will provide a foundation for future genome studies of the animal.
we have established and sequenced EST libraries for C. dromedarius and have generated a database for the sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have established a camel EST database that can serve as a resource for the scientific community to perform comparative studies and for the camel breeders and farmers to improve the health of their livestock.
the camel ESTs are useful for gene discovery and annotation, and that the CAGBASE database can serve as a valuable resource for future studies.
the camel is a good model for comparative genomic studies with other mammals and that it is possible to obtain a good coverage for camel genome with the current sequencing technologies.
